author: swain
title: Drop the chat message tables chat no longer uses
body:
`AgentMessage` has been chat's only message store since #3872, live in prod since 2026-11-18 19:50 UTC and clean through a 3-hour watch. That leaves `chat_message` and `chat_message_segment` with no reader and no writer: every row in them is a second copy of something `agent_message` already holds, and nothing has rewritten them in two deploys.

Keeping them costs real things. There are two places a message could be written, two orders it could be read in, and no way to tell from the schema which one is authoritative. `chat_message_feedback` also still hangs off a nullable pair — `chat_message_id` and `agent_message_id`, read everywhere with a fallback — so today a rating can technically name two different messages. Dropping the old tables is what lets the rating name exactly one.

So this drops them, in one migration. It is one PR rather than an expand-contract pair because no task can be serving a version of the app that touches these tables: the code that did was replaced in #3872, and I confirmed against deployed `main` that the only remaining references are integration-test fixtures, which never ship. The single thing a drop cannot repair is a rating whose `agent_message_id` the #3872 backfill left null — those are real ratings by real users, so the migration counts them first and raises instead of deleting them. Re-pointing them is a decision about user data, not something a migration should guess.

`ChatMessageRole` and `ChatMessageSegmentKind` stay on the Prisma schema. They name no table, but `@goodparty_org/contracts` generates the chat contract's enum schemas from the Prisma schema folder, and both are part of the response shape every chat client reads.

Two readers keyed to the old relation name rather than the old type name — the Chief of Staff first-conversation count and one dashboard fixture — turned up in the test run rather than in the grep, and are pointed at `agentMessages`.

-  assistant row of a turn. That is how the backfill stays idempotent and why

-

-
-- One scope at a time: five migrations of the same store, and ChatMessage
-  could only be dropped after the last.
-- A soak period: the flag already gives an instant rollback while both tables
-  are written.
-- Replaying raw tool results now: changes model cost and behaviour, which the
-  judge should settle separately.

@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+---
+title: Chat has one message table, so the tables it replaced are dropped
+status: active
+decided_by: [swain]
+date: 2026-11-19
+code: ['#3897']
+scope:
+  - packages/gp-api/src/chats/**
+  - packages/gp-api/prisma/schema/agentMessage.prisma
+  - packages/gp-api/prisma/schema/chatMessageFeedback.prisma
+supersedes: []
+superseded_by:
+---
+
+# Chat has one message table, so the tables it replaced are dropped
+
+## Decision
+
+`AgentMessage` is the only message table. `chat_message` and
+`chat_message_segment` are dropped, and `chat_message_feedback` keys on
+`agent_message_id` alone (NOT NULL, unique with the submitter).
+
+The drop is one PR, not a two-deploy expand-contract. Every task still serving
+traffic during the rollout of this deploy is already on #3872, which reads and
+writes neither table, so there is no version of the app left that a dropped
+table could break. The one thing a drop cannot repair is a rating whose
+`agent_message_id` the earlier backfill left null, so the migration counts
+those first and raises rather than deleting real feedback.
+
+`ChatMessageRole` and `ChatMessageSegmentKind` stay on the Prisma schema. They
+name no table, but `@goodparty_org/contracts` generates the chat contract's
+enum schemas from the Prisma schema folder, and both are in the response shape
+every chat client reads.
+
+## Context
+
+#3872 finished moving chat's readers and writers onto `AgentMessage` and was
+live in prod for a 3-hour watch before this. Keeping the old tables any longer
+costs a second backfill target, a second place a message can be written, and
+`chat_message_feedback`'s nullable double key — a rating row that can name two
+different messages and has to be read with a fallback.
+
+## Alternatives rejected
+
+- **An expand-contract split across two deploys**: extra deploys to protect
+  against a version of the app that no longer exists, since the migration that
+  added `agent_message_id` shipped two days before and its code path is gone.
+- **Dropping the enum types with the tables**: they are wire enums the chat
+  contract generates from, and dropping them breaks the contract build.
+- **Deleting rows whose `agent_message_id` is null**: those are real ratings by
+  real users; refusing the migration makes a human decide where they go.

diff --git a/packages/gp-api/prisma/schema/migrations/20261119100000_drop_chat_message/migration.sql b/packages/gp-api/prisma/schema/migrations/20261119100000_drop_chat_message/migration.sql

@@ -0,0 +1,39 @@
+-- Chat writes and reads only `agent_message` since #3872, so the two tables it
+-- replaced are dropped here. Every task still serving traffic during a rollout
+-- of this deploy is already on #3872, which touches neither table: there is no
+-- version of the app left that could read or write them.
+
+-- A rating has to name an AgentMessage once its ChatMessage key is gone, so a
+-- row left null by #3872's backfill would be silently lost. Refuse the drop
+-- instead: the count says how many, and re-pointing them is a decision about
+-- real feedback, not something a migration should guess.
+DO $$
+DECLARE
+    unrated bigint;
+BEGIN
+    SELECT count(*) INTO unrated
+    FROM "chat_message_feedback"
+    WHERE "agent_message_id" IS NULL;
+
+    IF unrated > 0 THEN
+        RAISE EXCEPTION
+            'chat_message_feedback has % row(s) with no agent_message_id; re-point them onto their AgentMessage before dropping chat_message',
+            unrated;
+    END IF;
+END $$;
+
+-- DropForeignKey
+ALTER TABLE "chat_message_feedback" DROP CONSTRAINT "chat_message_feedback_chat_message_id_fkey";
+
+-- DropIndex
+DROP INDEX "chat_message_feedback_user_message_unique";
+
+-- AlterTable
+ALTER TABLE "chat_message_feedback" DROP COLUMN "chat_message_id",
+  ALTER COLUMN "agent_message_id" SET NOT NULL;
+
+-- DropTable
+DROP TABLE "chat_message_segment";
+
+-- DropTable
+DROP TABLE "chat_message";
